history.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW no-text PNG mechanism illustration of dynamic graphs, for a Chinese textbook. The two supplied TGN paper crops explain memory and message roles; use them as content references, independently arrange this candidate. Wide clean landscape, ideally 2400 by 1350, with two clearly separated horizontal mechanism areas and ample genuine-font labeling space. No large global title.

TOP AREA: snapshot-time processing. Exactly THREE small flat graph snapshots at successive observation times. Each contains FOUR persistent circular node identities, with one designated blue node located at the same position in all three; change a small subset of edges between snapshots. One graph encoder BELOW each graph maps the current graph to the designated node's current neighbourhood representation. One separate temporal-memory update BELOW each representation combines that representation with the same node's previous memory. Connect the three memory updates horizontally LEFT TO RIGHT; keep node identity aligned through time. Use shared-appearance graph encoder modules, not three differently styled models. Leave short-label space in each module, for snapshot/time, encoder, and temporal-memory names. This area must visibly distinguish within-snapshot computation from observed time; reserve a small adjacent annotation area for the distinction, but do not add fake extra observations or spurious causal edges.

BOTTOM AREA: one observed interaction, explicit read-before-write order. On the left, a pair of PRE-EVENT memory objects feed an interaction scoring module; its score is an output, not the event itself. Later along the chronology, a distinct observed interaction between the same TWO nodes arrives, and only THEN a message-generation module reads the event and the pair of pre-event memories. Message generation feeds an aggregation module, aggregation feeds a memory-update module, and this update outputs a pair of POST-EVENT memory objects. Keep the PRE and POST pair distinguishable with pale blue versus pale green. The pre-event memories must also reach the message generator via a clean bypass arrow. There is no post-event-memory arrow into the earlier scoring module, and no score arrow into the event-arrival object. Keep the score branch and the observed-event source separate. A thin neutral chronology guide can distinguish before, event, and after stages; leave room for their actual-font captions. The actual interaction may be a simple short edge between two flat circles; no decorative calendar/clock badges needed.

Use meaningful graph nodes, flat memory strips and sparse message objects, not an all-card dashboard. White background with white modules and a few very pale semantic groupings. Lancet #7B95C6 blue for historical information and graph encoding, #F59C7C peach for event/score, #67A583 green for updated memories; pale uniform fills are 18% or 22% opaque white mixtures. Same node/module types consistent glyphs; maximum one icon per frame and no redundant decoration. Clear thin neutral-gray arrows and exact clean endpoints; no lines across reserved text areas.

No words, letters, numerals, formulas, pseudo-text, legends or watermark. Reserve headings adjacent to any mechanism glyph rather than centered far away. Pure white #FFFFFF canvas, uniform flat fill with no grain, paper/canvas texture, ripples, stripes, clouding, gradient, shadow, gloss, 3D or perspective. All glyphs and graphs are planar 2D. After generation, actual fonts will supply all Chinese, English, mathematical variables and annotations.

selected.prompt: Make a color-only edit of this exact no-text technical drawing. Preserve EVERY component position, margin, scale, all grids/row and column counts, node counts, connectors, arrow direction, line endpoints, layer glyphs and label whitespace. Never redraw its topology or rearrange content. Apply the palette to EVERY colored frame, fill, circle, bar, arrow and line; leave NO original high saturation pigment. Blue/cyan becomes muted #7188A3 and #E5EAF0; green #829C8B/#E8EEE9; yellow/orange #B4A16F/#F1ECDD; red/pink #A7787D/#F0E5E6; purple #9588A5/#ECE8F0. Use blue for main generic modules/output, red only for errors/loss or an indispensable distinct series. Ordinary boxes rounded about 6px. Background pure white; neutral wires #556170. No shadows, texture, gradients, letters, numbers, or pseudo text. Preserve exact canvas aspect ratio and all empty label spaces. Preserve natural input images and data point relations. All graph node circles use the SAME muted blue style; keep scientifically distinct node roles muted green/yellow sparingly.
